page: OVHcloud t2-le-180 is a KVM-based server within the Cloud GPU family. It features 60 dedicated physical cores powered by Intel Xeon 6226R processors running at a clock speed of 2.9 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is configured with 180.0 GB of system memory, yielding a ratio of 3.0 GB per core. For hardware acceleration, the server integrates four NVIDIA V100S GPUs from the Volta family, providing a combined total of 128 GB of VRAM. Local storage is provided by a 500 GB NVMe SSD, and network connectivity is supported by a 10 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark data highlights strong performance in parallel processing, memory throughput, and machine learning tasks. The server achieves a strong rating in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 324.83 GB/sec and a strong PassMark memory score of 2794.65. Its primary strength lies in large language model inference, where it registers top-tier performance across multiple model sizes. Specifically, it processes prompts at 15337.57 tokens/sec for a small 135M model, 1308.79 tokens/sec for a medium 7B model, and 152.1 tokens/sec for a large 70B model. Text generation speeds also reach top-tier levels, achieving 119.58 tokens/sec on the 7B model and 18.53 tokens/sec on the 70B model.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the t2-le-180 offers high resource density by bundling four enterprise-grade GPUs with a high physical core count on a single instance. This configuration is highly efficient for workloads that can fully parallelize across multiple GPUs and dedicated CPU cores. However, a potential tradeoff is the memory-to-core ratio of 3.0 GB per core, which may limit performance for memory-intensive datasets that do not fit within the 180.0 GB system memory or the 128 GB GPU VRAM.

This server is designed for GPU-accelerated workloads, including large language model inference, deep learning training, and parallel scientific simulations. The dedicated 60-core CPU architecture and 10 Gbps network bandwidth also make it suitable for high-throughput data processing, ray tracing, and multi-threaded decompression tasks.
